And as your scientists have stated, there is no possible means of destruction of energy forces. There can only be alterations in the form.

Then the voice changes, and Nona speaks. Greetings in the love and the light of the One Who is All. I am Nona. She takes up a question asked without words, on a subject shrouded in confusion. Divorce.

This is a phenomenon known only within certain tiny illusions, she says. Entirely within your society it is an artificial word, for it describes what happens when one piece of paper is replaced within your society's paper records with another piece of paper. Yet this happenstance causes a great deal of pain and difficulty among your peoples.

What she wishes to speak on, with compassion, is karma. When your holy works recommend that marriage be obtained throughout one lifetime, she says, it is recommended because it is likelier that you will correctly apply yourself to your karma if you have a controlled circumstance throughout one experience. It is likelier, if you engage in several karmic relationships within one experience, that there will be unsatisfied karma. It is simply more difficult to treat more people rightly than it is to treat one person rightly. Behind the law is the compassion of an all-loving Father.

In any experience with any karmic relationship, she says, it is necessary that your actions be founded in love. If an action which is founded in love results in the termination of that relationship, your karma has in no way been dissatisfied. If you remain with one person and yet your actions are not founded in love, then your karma won't be satisfied.

So you see, although the word divorce has great traumatic impression to give your peoples, the reality behind that word is what you make of it. You yourself, an individual upon your own path, learning through experiences with other souls. Think not of the paper but of the love. Think not of past mistakes but of your present chances to give love. If you have gone through many years thinking that two plus two are five, and then you discover that two plus two are four, you have corrected an error. Now two plus two are no longer five in your mind. Reality, and love, and correctness, are what you make of it now. Right now.

The point of stillness between the two sides. The love behind the paper. The knowing you already are. It was never far away.

Thank you for listening.

title: Love That Does Not Destroy
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: love that does not destroy.

It is the summer of nineteen seventy-six, and the one who calls himself Hatonn has something sharp to say about the most overused word on the planet. He is not scolding. He is diagnosing. Love, he says, has produced serious side effects down here. Hatred. War. Broken people. And he wants you to know that none of that came from love itself. It came from a misunderstanding of it.

He begins, though, with patience. He had opened the evening by inviting questions, then sensed the room holding back, thoughts not yet at the surface. His answer to the hesitation is worth keeping. In time, he says, with patience, the questions troubling you will become very clear. The confusion you feel is not a flaw in you. It is a feature of the illusion you are living in. Within it, what is actually a unity seems to be a process, and things seem to take time. It often seems, he says, that that which should be, is not, and that which should not be, is.

But listen to how they put it. The process is the illusion. And the illusion exists to instruct you in exactly one subject. That subject is love. So whatever problem is sitting on your chest right now, whatever seems out of place or overdue, Hatonn reframes it entirely. It is not a malfunction. It is the lesson, arriving in disguise.

And here he draws the line that changes everything. Love, as known upon your planet, is like the illusion itself: a process. It has a beginning and an end. From its creation to its destruction, it can take down the people who believed this was love, until they go indifferent and decide love is not all that there is. I love that he says this so plainly. Human love, as most of us practice it, has an expiration date built into it, and when it expires, people blame love instead of the packaging.

Then he holds up the other thing, the one he actually means. There is a love that is beautiful. It is not the human love. It is the love of the Creator. This love does not have limitation. It is not a process. It is, he says, simply the power that created you, the source from whence you came, and the ending to which you are irresistibly drawn. Yet the end is the endless beginning.

Sit with that for a moment. A love that has no process, no arc from creation to destruction. If you let that kind of love flow through you, he says, you do not go down to destruction in your relationships. You do not find an end to your patience. You do not become downhearted. Because this love is within you. Such a simple thing, he says, and yet so very difficult. That is why you are here. To learn how to tap into that love, even in the face of the illusion of your body and your life, which offer you again and again a chance to show what you know. That love is infinite.

Now the practical part, because Hatonn always brings one. It is impossible, he says, to tap into this love by pretending to on the human level. You cannot fake your way in with sentiment. The door is reached by stilling the process of body and mind that is occupying your attention. When your attention has been centered, not on the outer or on the mental, but on the inner planes, then the door may open, and love may come to you.

And here is the merciful part. Touching base like this does not require hours. It requires regularity. Do it often, and the pipeline will open, and you will see the results in your life. I love that word, pipeline. Not a lightning bolt. A pipeline.

Then he says something that lands hard on the religions of this planet. There are people, he says, who do this without knowing they are doing it. There are people who say many different things about what they are doing, and believe they are different from each other, and this is a great problem within your religions, for they believe that they are different from each other. The labels fight. The tapping is the same. And you can tell who has tapped it, he says. Not by their doctrine. By their joy. The sign of one who knows the Creator is joy, a burning steady kind that will not die. That person who is patient, these are the fruits, he says, of the love that does not destroy.

So there is your diagnostic, in one sentence. If you are not at this moment experiencing a joy that burns on steadily, meditate more. Take yourself away from your humanity and get in touch with love. It has gotten a very bad name upon this planet, he says, and yet in love you were created, and all that is powerful within you is of love.

Your future, he says, not in the physical sense but in the spiritual, lies completely in your attempts to seek that love. It is a simple quest. And we are with you, to help in any way.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Seed of Your Spirit
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the seed of your spirit.

A week into June of nineteen seventy-six, Hatonn arrives with a homework assignment for the eyes. Not the mind. The eyes. He says the group has passed an unending series of miracles just walking to the meeting that evening, trees and flowers and animals, creations of the Father all around them. But then he asks them to go further than that, past the intellectual admiration of beauty. He wants them to look at anything, a tree, a wall, a piece of cloth, a stone, and see it as what it actually is. Alive. Made of love.

Listen to how they put it. It does not matter what you choose to focus your attention upon, he says, for all things are alive. There is nothing that is without creative power and consciousness. Pay total attention, focused attention, to whatever you choose. When you can perceive trees and walls and stone as love, he says, then you will have begun to perceive things as they are.

Meditation is not an escape room, he says. It is a technique whereby the seeker becomes more aware of the creation as it truly is. But when you go forth from meditation, it is the world you open your eyes to that is to inform your knowledge. If you have knowledge and cannot apply it, then you have nothing.

And he is honest about the bar. The total end of your seeking within this illusion, he says, is to perceive the reality behind and within the illusion. You cannot do this, he says, simply by maintaining a reasonable amount of calm, although this is greatly desirable. Your perceptions of all that you see need to become transformed. Calm is the platform, not the goal.

Then he turns the homework inward, and this is where the session gets its title. The most central creation of the Father within your attention, he says, is yourselves. Each of you is a great treasure trove that you can observe. But you have to look at yourself the way you would look at a tree or a stone. Not something familiar. A strange and unusual object, to be looked at from a distance, from a perspective gained in meditation. You are alive, he says, through the power of love, and your real nature is hidden in the folds of that mystery.

Picture yourself, he says, as a seed. It is written in your holy works that the seed depends on the soil for whether it grows or not. Your spirit is a seed within you. All that it will become is already within it. But you must put it in the correct environment. It needs darkness, by which we mean meditation. It needs light and water. It needs space to grow, the space within your life that you make for your spirit.

I want to stay with that darkness line for a moment. Darkness, by which we mean meditation. The darkness of soil. Of a closed eye. The seed does not need your anxiety about whether it is growing. It needs you to tend it. You must give it, he says, the water and the sunlight of your attention. And the sunlight that will truly ripen the seed of your spirit, he says, is the attention you pay to what is happening to you. The trees that you pass. The people that you meet. The first-hand experiences of your life. You may make these things stony ground, or well-watered and warm earth, depending on where you put your attention.

He says, you may think it strange that we who are supposedly more advanced continue to use the language of simple farmers. And yet, he says, the simplest things are the things that never become foolish. The universe operates on the basis of cycles. And the life of your spirit is a bed to be nurtured just as surely as any other garden. As far as we know, that garden never gets beyond the point where it needs tending. Never. No graduation from the garden.

When Hatonn returns, he ties it together with the sentence that holds the whole evening. The life that has power, he says, the life that has begun to spring from the inside, from the core of your being, so that it is an enabling life, so that the person living it is able to give with love and with energy, this life is available to the seeker who has truly sought and found that which transforms his life. Within the religion many of you know, he says, this has been called being saved. And yet the Redeemer is your own consciousness.

You do not need to struggle from moment to moment, he says, from thought to thought, from action to action. You only think you do, because you have not been taking your meditation into your life. If you cannot do it all the time, do it once. And then do it again. Five seconds, one minute of focused concentration in the spirit is far more beneficial to you than you can imagine.

Five seconds. That is the whole assignment. Tend the seed. Look at the stone. Let the darkness do its work. And never fear, he says in his parting line, for those who seek will never be left without the Comforter.

Thank you for listening.

title: The New Age Is Here
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the new age is here.

June of nineteen seventy-six, and Hatonn opens the evening explaining why he has changed his tune. In the early years of contact, he says, the mission was mostly a warning. Your leaders could have brought your peoples, several times over, into a war far more devastating than any you can imagine, with devices capable of destroying your race. So they spoke strongly about the dangers. And the reason the tone changed, he says, is simple. The change is now with us.

Listen to how they put it. The new age is not coming, my friends. The new age is here. Where once they warned, now they inform. The changing vibrations of the planet are within your reach now, he says, and if you meditate and seek them, and if you add your strength to them, you may aid your planet with your love and your light, and from within help to go into this new age. You can now be full of strength, with no further need for the destructiveness.

And then he pays the group, and humanity with them, a compliment that lands like a weather report. It is a great blessing, he says, that your peoples have begun to build the strength of love within themselves. You are much, much stronger as a people now than you were ten of your years ago. And with each year, your strength increases, and the possibility of this destructiveness decreases. Ten years earlier they had found people weak in their ability to give love from within their own strength. Now, he says, the reserves are up.

He folds in a picture of death that reframes everything. The death you carry within you, he says, is only a minor transformation which frees the life within you to the next stage of development. So it is with this cycle of your planet. During the cycle your planet became ill, and called upon itself what you would call karma. But you are coming into a new cycle, where the body of your planet will be whole again. You still have the karma to alleviate, but it gets easier within the new vibration. This is your privilege, he says. And to a certain extent, ours.

The questions that night get sharper. One man asks the hard one. Is it right to be too passive? If pushed to the limit, is it right to react to violence, if that seems the only way open, or should passiveness go beyond that?

Hatonn will not give him a yes or no, and says so outright. The master known as Jesus set the ideal: there is no end to passivity. Yet the master accepted responsibility for his passivity, to the point of allowing his own death. Within your planetary sphere, he says, it is often very difficult to become a master capable of giving up his life to demonstrate total love. So they could never recommend this choice to any person. This choice is a private choice.

But then he gives the man something better than an answer. He gives him a technique. Mentally and forcefully, he says, remove yourself from the corner, and realize that you have a great deal of space about you that no one can violate. That time and space are an illusion, and you do not have one second in a crowded situation. You have an infinite amount of time and an infinite amount of space. And you are a creative consciousness, capable of bringing to bear on this situation a creative solution which neither causes you to show a lack of love, nor causes you to betray those who depend upon you.

And then the sentence I keep returning to. See yourself, he says, as a dancer upon a great wide plain, with the situation a step in the dance. To this person, a creative solution will often recommend itself. It is a difficult question to answer, he admits, for your vibration is a very intense one. It is easy for us to say, and hard for you to do. We are with you, he says, and all of the forces of light are at your disposal.

The one known as Laitos takes the floor briefly after. His message is short and practical. The abilities you seek are dormant within you, asleep for many, many lifetimes. The barriers are accepting that the communication is real, setting aside the analysis of what you receive, and having the concepts in your own mind to carry it. And the law beneath it all: in order to attain anything which is desired, the realization that it is becoming is the initial step. Know it is manifesting, practice patience, and in due time it shall be. You have within you the abilities, he says. You do not need to look outward.

The evening closes with a voice that will not give a name, only that it is of this planet, asking the group to send their light to California for the next few months. The inner planes function in advance of the physical, it says, and what is harmonized there can be averted here.

From warning to welcome. From danger to strength. The new age is not a date on a calendar. It is a vibration you join by adding your love to it.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Rainbow Bridge
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the rainbow bridge.

Late June, nineteen seventy-six. Hatonn begins with a story, one of the loveliest in this archive. Once there was a boy who was puzzled by the thing the grown-ups kept calling love. He asked his parents what love was. They said, love is honoring your father and your mother, and obeying them. He tried that. He was not satisfied.

He asked his teacher. Love is doing what the teacher tells you, and learning what you are asked to learn. True, perhaps. But not satisfying.

He asked his friend. His friend said, I am not sure, but I have noticed that when people want something, they say, I love you. And the boy thought, perhaps this is closer to what love is than anything I have heard.

Then he fell asleep. He sailed away in a ship with wide, billowing sails, over a rainbow bridge into the far waters, and the ship harbored itself upon a white beach. He walked into a softly forested place, and there he saw a beautiful entity in white robes, glistening golden, not with sunlight, but with light coming from the face of the entity itself.

He asked the radiant being, sir, tell me, what is love? And the being said not a word. He knelt down and looked into the little boy's eyes. The boy looked back into those luminous eyes. And suddenly his own eyes were changed, and the world was transformed wherever he looked. Every mote of sand danced with an energy so joyful it was indescribable to him. And yet he knew. It was love.

No lecture. No definition. Just a look. The being said not a word, but led him back to his ship. He sailed over the rainbow bridge and back to his bed. In the morning he remembered. He looked around his room, and his room was transformed. His mother came in, and he ran to her and hugged her, and said, I love you. And he saw his mother transformed into a being that was love. He ran to his teacher and said, teacher, I love you. And the teacher became gentle, compassionate, and human, in his eyes alone. Each thing that he looked at with his eyes of love sent love back to him, for it was all made of love. And the little boy no longer needed to ask what love was.

I keep thinking about why the being said nothing. A definition would have been another thing to obey, another rule from another adult. Instead the boy was given changed eyes. Love, Hatonn says when the story ends, is so simple that it cannot be described. It can only be experienced. If you will be as a child, and when you open your eyes, if you will give to the world your love, the world will give you back love. It is a process of recognition of what really is. Nothing more.

The rest of the evening is the instruction manual for getting those eyes back. The greatest distorter, Hatonn says, is the intellect through which you perceive. You are the master of that which affects you. You are the helmsman of the intellect. If it were not important, he says, it would not have been given to you. But it must be disciplined, and open to the reception of the Creator. In meditation, the intellect is stilled, and the simplicity of things as they are seeps into your subconscious. Within yourself there is a sea, he says, over which meditation erects a rainbow bridge. On the other side lies a part of yourself which is illumined and radiant, and wishing only to bring the rest of you unto him.

Your own bridge, built nightly, to the part of you that already knows. Contact that portion of yourself, he says. Love is an extremely simple thing.

He draws a hard line about what love is not. In this illusion, love is associated with objects, and it is felt that if one loves, then one gives things. Yet when one truly loves, one gives of oneself. When a loved one does not give you the desired things, you may say that love has failed. Yet look to yourself, he says, and seek to give of yourself in love, not to others' expectations, but to your own highest understanding. For what you give, you shall surely receive. All in reality is love, if you can but see it. And most importantly, if you can but act it out. Love-in-action is the reason for which you are here. You are in an arena, a magnificent arena. And the challenge lies in your actions.

Each of you are perfect beings, he says. You have come into existence as an act of love and perfection of the Creator. All imperfections are indeed the creations of man. Recognize your divinity, and envision your perfection. Fear not the reaction of others upon your actions. For you to act in all honesty, with all sincerity, to the best of your ability, is what you are to do. Some will misunderstand. Some will not. Fear not. Recognize only the divinity, and understand that it is their confusion which they reflect.

Be as a child. Open your eyes. Give the world your love, and watch it give love back.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Perfect Leaf Within
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the perfect leaf within.

The middle of July, nineteen seventy-six. Hatonn opens with four sentences that could serve as the whole session. I am love, my friends. You are love. And we are one. To give you a sense of the immediacy of that truth is very difficult, he says, and yet unless love is alive and immediate in your experience, you may search forever without truly understanding the object of your search.

Then he takes the group outside, to a tree beside the dwelling. Look at its leaves, he says. Some are almost perfect. Symmetrical. Beautifully green. No mark or damage. On the same tree, other leaves have been damaged by insects, or have grown crooked, or their color is not as expected. And yet, he says, these are not good leaves and bad leaves. For within them, each, is the same perfect leaf, which is not separate from the leaf, as an ideal, but is within that leaf, and is the true reality of that leaf.

Listen to how they put it. The perfect leaf is not separate from the damaged leaf, as an ideal off somewhere. It is within it. It is the true reality of it. Then he tries clouds. The many, many forms of clouds. Some bring storms, some are simply beautiful. Yet good and bad cannot be said of clouds, he says, for they are all perfect in their cloudness. Perfect in their cloudness. What a phrase.

And you yourself, he says, are in essence a perfect version of you, whether your manifestation may be good or bad within the illusion. The ideal that created you is immediately within you. It is present within you at this time, and it is informing and inspiring your every breath. And this is true of all those you meet, no matter what their manifestations.

It seems like a cliché to say this to you, he admits, and yet you will never be free of turmoil until you are able to bring into your conscious experience the knowledge of oneness in love that you can find in meditation. Without meditation, it is not likely you would ever discover that unity with the Creator that is the wellspring of true love. And without repeated seeking of this unity, it is very difficult to advance in bringing love into your immediate experience.

But here is the part the group needed most, I think. In addition to the meditation, he says, you need to bring that feeling into your life as you live it, moment by moment. And he gives them a practice, almost embarrassingly personal. Attempt to form a personal relationship with the Creator, he says. Seek him as you would a trusted friend. Love him as you would love the most beloved friends you could ever have. True emotion that comes from the heart, personal, deep-felt emotion, is necessary, in order to bring to your consciousness the realization that in the Creator you are dealing with the single most important relationship of your life.

Let the love for the Creator build and become more and more personal, more and more real, more and more felt. And then, he says, take that sweet feeling and live it day to day. Feel the immediacy of that Creator, and share it with the people you meet. This is the secret, he says. If you can approach each person as someone who is the Creator, and whom you may be privileged to serve, your troubles will sort themselves out before you. For love is always reflected in love.

That last line does so much work. Love is always reflected in love. Not earned. Reflected.

Through a second instrument that evening, Hatonn adds the warning that completes the practice. Change, he says, can only take place within yourself. And a great part of love is understanding. Do not judge another, he says. That is reserved for the One who has made us all. If we look upon another to disagree, we cannot truly give a loving hand to this being's free will. Remember the leaves. The damaged one is not a bad leaf. The crooked one is not failing at being a leaf. It is perfect in its leafness.

The questions that night circle dreams. One man asks what his dreams have to do with his feelings about reality. Hatonn's answer is simple and worth keeping. Your consciousness has no beginning and no end, and as sleep is in its way a brief foretaste of death, the consciousness has no part of sleep. It is doing something all the time. Dreams are a partial record of the activity of the spirit, he says, a reliable communication from spirit to conscious self of the true development of the spirit's personality. Keep a record. When you awaken, immediately write down what you can remember, and as you practice, you will improve.

All of this is one teaching wearing different clothes. The perfect leaf within the damaged leaf. The Creator within the trusted friend. The spirit within the dream. The love within the love. The immediacy is the point. It is not far away. It is not after death. It is informing and inspiring your every breath, right now, in the damaged, crooked, beautiful leaf of your life.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Original Vibration
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the original vibration.

July twenty-fifth, nineteen seventy-six. Hatonn begins with the physics of the whole archive, in one sentence. Love, he says, is the word which created all that there is. What vibration is to the physical world, love is to the consciousness that created the physical world.

Then he proves it with an analogy your scientists would recognize. All things are made up of vibration and energy centers. Yet to you, the manifestations seem many and varied: tables and buildings and trees and human bodies. Yet all of these, he says, are one thing: energy in motion. And so it is with love. Each thought that you have was originally purely of love. Yet man, as well as the Creator, is a creator, and man has invented many complexities which take love and cause it to form many and various shapes.

Anger. Distress. Resentment. Irritation. We treat these as forces opposed to love. Hatonn says they are not opposites at all. They are derivatives of love, man-made forms, contortions. And here is the sentence to carry home. In your holy works it has been written that the way to defeat evil is to meet it with love. This is true, he says, because the original vibration of love is always stronger than its derivative, man-made forms. The original always wins. That is not a hope. That is physics.

To realize that all you see is love, he says, is to find peace. No longer need you feel anger and distress. These derivatives can be replaced in your thinking by a consciousness of the basic true love, the all-loving, all-serving, all-creative emotion that surrounds and inspires each of you.

And how do you find this fountainhead? As always, meditation. For clever as man's minds are, he says, they are often too clever, and in their cleverness men have devised many strange contortions of love. In meditation, as you lay down these man-made concepts and open yourselves to your deeper identity, the basic reality of the love that created you can make contact with you in your conscious mind. And as you come in contact with love as it really is, you gain strength to look the world of man-made emotions in the face and say, ah, but I know a deeper and truer way to express love.

I love that line. It is not a weapon. It is a recognition. You touch base with this creative love on a regular basis, and little by little your being begins to transmit that love, and you become what you seek to become: an instrument for the love of the Creator.

You are in the world, as it has been said, he continues, but you are not of the world. You are a divine being, dwelling within the body of the so-called human. And this human will have a very short life, and yet the divine being that is your true higher self will exist eternally. Seek to unify your consciousness as a human with your higher identity as a portion of the divinity of the Creator, through meditation.

Through a second instrument that evening, the message turns practical, and a little stern. It is you who creates all that you experience, he says. It is you who must accept the love. And then the warning that lands like a physics law. Be cautious of that which you project toward your fellow man and toward the universe, for you are the Creator, and that which you project shall indeed come into existence, and it shall also travel back and affect you, for you are the Creator, and you must live within your creation.

You must live within your creation. That is the whole moral argument of the session in seven words. No one else can create your experience for you. You may share in the experiences of others. You may dwell within experiences others created. But the projection is yours, and the echo comes home.

Desire gets its own brief treatment before the contact falters. Truly, he says, what you desire, you shall obtain, if the desire is of a strong enough vibration. Not a casual wish. A vibration. The wanting has to be tuned, sustained, strong enough to move the field. Then it manifests.

And the evening ends with a small, strange gift. One of the instruments speaks up, a little embarrassed, and says that while he was speaking about love, he received an impression he could not quite find words for. A definition of love, arriving mid-sentence. And this is what came through. Luminescence omnipresent, vacillating eternally. Carla's response, caught on the tape, is perfect. That's easy for you to say.

I have been turning that phrase over ever since I read it. Luminescence omnipresent. Light everywhere. Vacillating eternally. Moving, pulsing, never still. Not a substance but a shimmer. That is what love is, according to the impression. Not a feeling you have. A light you are inside of, which never stops moving.

The original vibration is always stronger than its derivatives. So when the day brings you the contortions, anger, irritation, the strange shapes love takes when we get clever with it, you can look them in the face and say, ah, I know a deeper and truer way. The fountainhead is still there. It was never anywhere else.

Thank you for listening.

title: Eat the Fruit, Plant the Seed
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: eat the fruit, plant the seed.

August eighth, nineteen seventy-six. Hatonn comes with a parable about fruit, and it does more work than most sermons. Experience, he says, is like eating a piece of fruit. The piece of fruit, being the experience, has an edible part which you immediately take into your system. When you finish the easily eaten part, you are left with the seed. And this, he says, you throw away.

Listen to how they put it. While the flesh of the fruit will feed your body for a day, if you do not plant the seeds you will not reap the long-term benefits of the living consciousness. In experience, what you taste in the moment is much like the flesh of the fruit. It may be sweet, in which case you eat it greedily, savoring every morsel. It may be sour, in which case you will not eat it, or only eat part of it. In either case, whether sweet or sour, the seed is the important part for your progress. In each experience there is a seed of wisdom, a lesson implicit in the experience, which you must plant in your consciousness in order to progress.

Sweet or sour, the seed is the seed. We sort experiences by taste. Hatonn says to sort them by seed.

So how do you plant it? Taking your experiences into meditation is very important, he says. Offering them up to the consciousness within you, not in a judgmental way, but simply as a desire that you truly learn from each experience, not just for the day, but for the future of your spirit. And on the level of the intellect, he offers a question to carry around with you. Ask yourself, with regard to your experiences: in this experience, was I of service? In this experience, did I want to be of service? For the seed which will enable you to progress rapidly, he says, has as its key love expressed in action. And the closest we can come to giving you this concept is the concept of service.

Service, he adds, is not always a thing. It is most often an attitude. To be of service is often simply to be non-judging, to be loving, to be willing to see the possibility of the Christ-consciousness in another. Bring that attitude into an experience, he says, and you have planted the seed as well as eaten the fruit. And when you take into meditation the experiences in which you did not manage it, even your failures will teach you.

The world itself, he says, will never progress, for you are the world. Only you can progress. You cannot influence the world, and most especially you cannot influence the Creator. Yet this is not necessary. For the world is as darkness and the Creator is light. If you can ask the Creator to influence you, it will be as light turned upon darkness, and the darkness will be no more.

You cannot move the world. You can only ask the light to move you.

He had opened the evening on progression itself. You have done well, he says. But once upon the path you cannot sway from one side to another. And there is a trap he names gently. For some, it is enough to obtain knowledge of this path and to sit idly by. But to grow ever stronger, you, like ourselves, must aid others. The teaching is not finished when it is understood. It is finished when it is given.

The questions that night include a beautiful one about children. Children, as well as adults and old people, are spirits, he says. Extremely vulnerable in the physical, yet as eternal and as complete as anyone on the planet. And then the line for every parent. More than what you do as your child grows, it will be what you are which affects his understanding and his progress. If you truly seek the spiritual, and live your life according to the path you seek, if every day you make room for spiritual seeking, your child will understand from the very beginning the purpose of life. It is never necessary to encourage a small, growing being to choose one way or another. It is only necessary for a child to know that there is such a thing as the spiritual path, and that it has given joy to those who are closest to him.

Beyond the giving of love, he says, that whole and complete being you have been given to care for will express to you himself what he will need. You do not have to sculpt the child. You have to be the path, visibly and joyfully, and let the child find it.

The closing words of the evening are an encouragement and a timeline. Trust yourself, he says. Please, trust yourself. Have confidence. In every sincere impulse, every honest desire to progress, let that have weight within you. Take yourselves seriously, and let the joy you feel from time to time take root and grow, until your life is transformed by your understanding of love. It will happen, he says. Not all at once. It is a progression.

Thank you for listening.

title: Let Love Live Your Life
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: let love live your life.

Mid-August, nineteen seventy-six. Hatonn arrives with a lesson about sharing. You carry, he says, the accumulation of all knowledge, not only from this life but from all lives before it, and it is constantly available. Meditation is the doorway. And it is your obligation to bring forth the purest manifestation: to share your knowledge, your experiences, and your love.

But he is careful here. There are many with whom sharing this knowledge would be useless, or harmful to the relationship. With those, he says, you can still share the love which is the total manifestation of those experiences and of that knowledge. Where words would wound, love can still be given. It just changes form.

The spoken word carries much power, he says, yet the unspoken word is even greater. You can send to all around you all the knowledge you contain by simply projecting your love to them. For love is the total manifestation of all your experience and knowledge. To direct that love, purely and completely, to any individual, is to share all that you contain. And you contain all the knowledge of the universe.

Each one of you, he says, is as a beacon upon the shore to guide the ships at sea. Shine brightly. Never allow your flame to dim, to flicker, to be extinguished. Allow your flame to glow brilliantly, wherever you are, and in whatever you do, and this indeed is enough. Do not be harsh upon yourself for faltering. You cannot falter when your focus is in the right direction. This is the law, he says. That which you desire you shall receive. Doubt it not, and it shall be fulfilled.

When you seek to know the source of love, he says, it is an attempt to become one with that which is infinite and invisible, nearer to you than your own body. You need go nowhere. Love is waiting for you, so close. The request, in its simplicity, is a willingness to turn your life over to love, to turn your life over to Christ-consciousness. You do not have the power to show love, he says. You can only offer your life to love, so that love can live your life.

All the will in the world cannot find the way of love, he says. But allow love to flow through you, without judgment and without hindrance, and it will teach you its ways, and it will live your life. You cannot direct the Creator. As long as you attempt to direct him, he will stand knocking, asking to be let into your heart. Seek and ye shall find. Knock and the door shall be opened. Truer words were never written.

And then, almost as an aside, the mirror teaching. When something in another person irritates you, look past it. What irritates you in another is a projection of what you either contain, or fear that you may contain, within yourself. You are the creator of your universe. You perceive within it that which you choose to perceive. It is your ship and you are the captain. And the assignment: you are to love all that you have created.

The second half of the evening belongs to a voice heard rarely in this archive, the one who calls himself Lattoo. Someone asks what happens to animals. Do they evolve like us? Each type of animal, Lattoo says, begins as a pool of consciousness, a general animal-ness. Through many incarnations, experiences mold an individual personality. And it is especially common, he says, for the domesticated animal to become individualized, through the love which they share with their masters. At that point, the animal no longer returns to the pool upon death. He begins the human type of evolution. In the spirit, this individualized animal will spend time dwelling upon the love of his master, and will incarnate, often, in order to be with his master.

The love you share with an animal is not sentiment. It is evolution.

Someone asks about places of power, like Findhorn in Scotland. Findhorn, Lattoo says, is not an electromagnetic phenomenon. It is a phenomenon of consciousness. One does not have to be sitting on top of the pyramid to get the energy, he says, for with consciousness, one can move the pyramid. It is the faith of the individual which builds the energy which makes the miracles possible. And then the sentence to carry. The place whereon you stand is holy ground. That power came, and does come, from the consciousness of love, which is the source of power for all things.

And to the worried one, the one whose thoughts will not stop at bedtime, Lattoo prescribes laughter. Remember, he says, that life as you know it is a cosmic joke. All of your busy thoughts and all of your worries are, at best, little cartoons. When you pass from this physical existence, you will spend some time laughing and some time crying. And the tears will come because you took things so seriously that you forgot to laugh and praise the Creator that gave you this marvelous cartoon. Do not forget to laugh.

Offer your life to love, and let love live it. Shine, and do not dim. And do not forget to laugh.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Comforter Comes in Silence
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the Comforter comes in silence.

August twenty-second, nineteen seventy-six. The first instrument struggles to hold the contact, and Hatonn explains why through another. The intellect of man is like a radio receiver, he says. It can receive external thought forms. But to receive and to analyze before attempting to transmit is to cause confusion in the energies. Analysis before transmission jams the signal.

Once the contact steadies, Hatonn states the mission in its simplest form. This is what we have for you, he says. A gift of knowledge and understanding. This is all that we bring. There is nothing more. No rescue. No technology. No salvation from outside.

The gift that night is oneness. Each thing, he says, is as a molecule within the body of the universe. You know how every particle of your physical form matters to its functioning. And so it is within the universe. Each individual, each particle, is of vast importance to the existence of this creation.

All of us have instilled within us the love by which we were created, he says. One form of love, one source, and that is the Creator. We are the projections and the practice of that love. As we are in him, so also is he within us. All things are interdependent. All things in truth are each other, and are one.

But to understand this with the intellect alone, he says, is limited. The intellect is contained within the physical form, and within that form abides your essence, your being. Your being is the manipulator of the form. You are the commander of the ship. Know thyself, he says. Know you, the manipulator of your form. And from this, you shall know the Creator. To you, he says, it is I, and we call it love.

Then the warning about the tool itself. That which you know as your intellect and that which we term the mind of the Creator are not very related concepts. Make that useful tool work for you, he says, rather than you working for it. Both the body and the mind crave instant and continuous attention. And if you, as a spiritual self, are not careful, you will be a slave to their requests, and will not allot any serious time to your progress outside the physical.

I keep coming back to that. The body and the mind crave instant and continuous attention. That is their job. Your job is to not be their slave.

Your scriptures say it is not a good thing to raise up graven images. Yet a graven image does not have to be made of earth or stone. It can also be made of words. And all those who say, I believe in the Father, or love has come into my life and will heal me, are kneeling to a graven image, for words have never done anything for anyone. To allow the experience of love to come into your life is to open yourself to it and to listen for it, for the understanding without words, the experience without intellect, is what will indeed show you love.

The Creator does not speak with you in human terms. The Comforter comes to you in silence. If you wish to heal or to help, pray only that you may listen and hear the voice of love. Do not expect gifts. Pray only that all of those upon your planet may feel this love. For true love does not discriminate. It is a unifier. Sit in silence, and open yourself to the energy that flows from love itself, through you and back again, out into the creation.

Is the antichrist born? Hatonn dissolves the question. There is no such concept, he says. The individual your peoples might call the antichrist is, in fact, the Creator, as are you and all of your peoples. The concept is simply the individualization of thought, the isolation from the whole. A parable of what happens to those who separate themselves in consciousness from the unity which is their actual reality.

Don asks his question without speaking it, telepathically, testing the contact. The answer is not the one he asked, but the one he needed. The Creator has shown them many things, Hatonn says, but not the rhythm and tempo of doings, for all things are free to form their own destinies. Their predictions are probability curves, more accurate as the moment draws near. Picture a rose, he says, as it grows on the bush. The day of its opening is not known. Only its shape when it does open.

The closing words of the evening are the ones I would put on the door of the whole series. We ask you to consider our words, he says, not as truth, but as an interesting thought to be considered by your discriminating mind. We are in no way infallible or perfect. We are as you, foolish beings attempting to learn, striving to be a little better than we were yesterday. We are a little ahead of you on the path of evolution, and we reach a hand very gladly to give you a pull up. It is a long path, my friends, but we have found great joy in it, and we know that it is there for you also.

Thank you for listening.

title: Through You, Not From You
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: through you, not from you.

The last Sunday of August, nineteen seventy-six. Hatonn tells the newcomers not to clutch what they hear as the whole truth. Listen, evaluate, and do with it as you please. Then he gets to the teaching. No finite entity, he says, neither yourselves nor we, your brothers, can love. Not can show love. Can love. The finite self cannot do it at all.

Then what are we supposed to do? To show love, he says, is simply to act as an open channel through which the healing waters of love can flow. Through you, not from you, to all that you touch. You are not the spring. You are the streambed.

And here is why trying harder makes it worse. If you think and concentrate upon your movements in attempting to perform complex tasks, he says, it is almost certain that you will stumble. For in your very thinking, you will have limited the instincts of your physical being. It is also true in the mental sphere. If you attempt too hard to organize and analyze your thoughts, they will disintegrate into splinters which have very little meaning. It is very difficult sometimes to make decisions, he says, because you are thinking too hard.

Most especially on the spiritual plane, he says, if you attempt to draw love from your own being, you will almost immediately run into very deep trouble. You see that your fingers end at the tips of your fingernails. You do not see that you are one with the air that surrounds them. From the very beginning you were taught that the thoughts which originate in your mind have been created only by you. You were not taught that thought comes from a beautiful, infinite mind, and that the thoughts that pass through you, although heavily diluted, are shades of that perfect thought.

So stop drawing from the well of yourself. There is no water in it. Open the channel instead. And how do you come in contact with the spring? For the reason of coming in contact with love, he says, we so often urge you to meditate. The Creator is everywhere you may go. If you go down to the doors of what you call Hell, the Creator is there. You cannot close your eyes, or your fingers, or your minds, and rid yourself of the Creator. Love is within you and all about you. If you do not recognize it, yet it is still there.

Then he says the sentence that might be the most freeing in this whole archive. It is not at all important that you have any belief or faith, he says. This means less than nothing. Know you only that as the sun shines from heaven, there is a power in the universe that gives life. You do not need to be faithful or believing. You need only be quiet and listen. Take these periods of silence on a daily basis, and evaluate your life after having meditated for a period of two of your months. It will begin to be apparent that the listening is making your day-to-day existence more loving.

Two months of quiet. Then check the results. It is an experiment, not a creed.

Earlier in the evening he had laid the foundation. You are, he says, the extension of the Creator, individually expressed, yet universally united. From that source you have been projected, yet there is a cord that shall extend forever, that shall never be broken, and through that cord flows the knowledge and the being of your Creator. You may tap the knowledge of the universe by going within yourself and meeting with the divinity within you. Know thyself, your holy book says. This does not mean knowing the intellect, which many of you consider yourselves to be. It does not mean knowing the ego. It means knowing the I AM, the God, the Creator within you. For that you truly are. You are united and inseparable from your Creator. No matter how hard you would choose to try, you can never be out of his presence.

He closes with service for the ones who will not take it. There are those that do not desire your service at the present time, he says. Yet the service you can render them silently, from purely a conscious basis, is immense. Silently offer those who would not request your service your love, your light, and your understanding, for they are receptive to your thoughts, whether they recognize it or not. You have planted the seed of love within that individual. And thus, you have served him.

Imagine yourself standing in a field of flowers, he says, the light shining down upon you, the birds singing, the fragrance of the flowers all about you. You stand in the love of the Creator, and if you open the windows of your spirit, you offer the beacon of that light to all that you meet. It may not be in very dramatic ways. It may be in a tiny little thing. Love is not anywhere else, he says. Love is here, in whatever situation you are, in whomever you meet, in all emotions and in all circumstances. See the love. See the creative power. See the healing. Meditate, and then open those eyes.

Thank you for listening.

title: You Are the Path
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: you are the path.

September fifth, nineteen seventy-six. It seems, he says, as though a certain quantity of intellectual information will constitute the knowledge you need. Yes, he says, you are on the path. But you are the path. You are that which the Creator may flow through.

It is written in your holy works, he says, that the one known as John the Baptist cried in the wilderness, make straight the way of the Lord. Each of you is a tangle of chaotic thoughts and actions, memories and hopes. And your one goal is to make a pathway, a straight way, for love to flow through. You will never organize that which you call your self, he says. Your physical self is an unruly thing. Yet within you there is a pathway, and as you meditate, you may seek and find it, and open yourself to it, and lo, the crooked will become straight, and the uncrossable mountains of your life will become as plains.

You see, he says, we assume that that which you are seeking, you are. For what you may be seeking, though it may seem an infinite amount of knowledge, is in fact a truth of such total simplicity that you, sitting there now, embody it totally. A truth so simple that many of your kind have missed it. This truth is that all things are one. That all is love. Its understanding is the straight way.

That which you seek, you already are. Be still, and begin to discover yourself. And watch for the trap of power. You can easily perceive those things you are having trouble with as powers against you, he says, and see yourself as needing a power to overcome them. But nothing has power. You may think that in healings the spirit overcomes the power of disease. Yet if there were a power to disease, he says, then there would be no possibility of its being healed. In truth, the consciousness of love is not power. It is simply the understanding that there is no power, but that all is one.

Listen to how they put it. Instead of reckoning from the standpoint of power against power, keep in your consciousness the truth that there is no power, that there is only love, so that you see those things that are difficult for you as a type of love which you may understand if you contemplate it, and which you can love in return. Since you do not recognize the illusory power of your difficulties, they do indeed begin to disperse, sometimes in very unexpected ways.

Sometimes, he says, a situation which you felt had power against you may stay just as it was before, yet in your consciousness you now understand that there is no power in that situation, but only love. And this understanding transforms your experience. Many things occur by interpretation only, within your mind, so that if love can be applied and the idea of power removed, the problem disappears.

The problem disappears not because the world changed, but because the interpretation did.

Through another instrument that evening, Hatonn takes up trouble itself. Everything that happens around you, he says, is caused by your desires, and everything you have desired will eventually come to pass. If you were immediately given everything you desired, it would not mean anything to you for very long, for you appreciate only that which you have worked for. Whenever you are confronted with a challenge you do not understand, think first of what the reason might be for this obstacle, what you might learn from it. If you put these sorrows in their right perspective, you will find, even in the deepest pit, that there is indeed a light up above that you may climb to.

Many allow themselves to become stagnant, he says, because they do not face their troubles and deal with them. And this help cannot be given to others, he adds, until you yourself have dwelt within this light and love. Since love is all there is, he says, there can be no sorrow. You yourself have put this name upon the experience you are passing through.

The evening closes with the one known as Laitos, on the energy the Confederation sends. Each of them is here for one reason only: to send you our love. They send a conditioning wave, designed to enhance your own meditative wave. Your brain, he says, is very much like a radio, capable of receiving and sending on various frequencies. They enhance the spiritual frequencies, so you can pick up, in a much stronger sense, the spiritual thoughts coming to you. And they are not the only voices on that wavelength. Meditating, you tune into the source closest to you, which is your own higher self. You have guides, he says, such as you would call angels, watching over you. You have not ever been, and will never be alone.

You need only request it mentally, he says. And if the vibration is uncomfortable, request that it be discontinued, and it will be. For that which you desire is above all things important to us.

You are the path. There is no power but love. The light is above the pit. You have never been alone.

Thank you for listening.

title: Your Life as a Work of Art
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: your life as a work of art.

September nineteenth, nineteen seventy-six. Hatonn begins with the teachers, and the one they keep coming back to. The Confederation has sent intermediaries onto your plane for centuries, he says, who acted as teachers among your peoples. Many were greatly misunderstood, even that one with whom you are so familiar who bears the name of Jesus. He taught that you are also the children of the Father that sent him. He taught oneness and equality. He demonstrated the abilities of the consciousness, and informed those about him that it was within their capabilities to do likewise. And this, Hatonn says, is one of the greatest truths which was not comprehended, and which has not been utilized or taught in the proper manner throughout the centuries since.

You are his thought patterns projected throughout the infinite universe. You cannot be separated from him, nor can you be separated from one another. And that instant closeness with a stranger? It is nothing other, he says, than recognizing within them the true identity of yourself.

Then he turns to the cycle. You are presently ending a cycle of time of existence, he says, and the planet is presented with the opportunity to transmute its entire physical form into a higher vibratory field. And you, as an individual, must also earn that right, through the raising of consciousness. Seek and you shall find, he says, as the master has said. Ask and you shall receive that which you desire. But be careful for what you ask, for your very thoughts are the creation of your experience. Guard your thoughts. And learn, most importantly, to go within yourself and achieve the union with that portion of the Creator's consciousness that lies within your being.

You are the perfect manifestation, he says, of that which you have chosen to be. It is your choice. It is your evolution. It is your experience. And it is yours to do with as you would choose.

Your will and your desire and your efforts are all-important, he says. You will get what you desire. Therefore, desire carefully and constantly. But effort alone will not give you wisdom. For mankind can work and work, but without the spirit, the soul that is within him, he will achieve nothing but weariness.

Effort is only the seed, he says. The fruition comes in meditation. The fruition comes when, in your desire, you stop talking and begin listening. Your physical ears are beset day and night by noise and more noise. So to protect yourselves you are constantly thinking, constantly generating a defensive wall of selfhood. But as long as you are thinking and talking, you cannot contact that wisdom that is within you, that is sleeping. So we say to you, seek, and then in your seeking, meditate.

Then he draws the small picture. You are an entity that has lived forever and will live forever, he says, dwelling in a tiny little ball that circles a sun in a very small corner of a totally infinite universe. And you are in a classroom that is much like a circus, with many things to see, and you are observing and attempting to learn. The energy that created all of the wrong thoughts was originally love. Those conceived in love have by their free will chosen to separate themselves into thoughts that are not of love, but are dark shadows across the face of love.

See yourselves as the generators of your own destiny, he says. If you will see your life as a work of art, you will stop thinking that life is something that happens to you, that you are the recipient of various good and bad things. And when your emotions and your words and your gestures begin to form a harvest of what you are learning in meditation, then you have made the great step. Then you may begin to become more confident of graduating from this school, of getting out of this rat race. When you leave your physical form, as you all will, and look back, you will see this life just as you would see a work of art. And you will see whether you have written badly or well. It matters not if you make mistakes. You can but learn. And each attempt to show what you have learned will sound a chord within your lifestream that is very sweet.

The days may seem to move very slowly when you feel under fire by a hostile world. But your life is short, he says. You are standing on a ball and you are learning. Connect with that source of love, a source which is rich in humor, a source in which you can relax and trust that there is no power on Earth as great as love. For that which you give from your inner spirit is the only reality for you.

And the final word of the evening, for anyone who feels trapped. There is no situation in which there is not freedom, he says. That which is bound by the Earth is only bound in illusion. Never consider yourself bound, for your imagination will take you away. Make the place for yourself that you desire in your mind, and go there.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Miracle Is Very Near
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the miracle is very near.

September twenty-sixth, nineteen seventy-six. Hatonn speaks to the men of Earth in sorrow. What we offer you, he says, is more precious than any treasure you can imagine. And yet we mourn that so few know of the treasure of love. You spend your time seeking after so many things that do not advance you on your spiritual path. What we offer you, he says, is more precious than any treasure you can imagine. And yet we mourn that so few know of the treasure of love. You spend your time seeking after so many things that do not advance you on your spiritual path.

But if you know who you are, at all, you can begin at this moment to seek out the miracle which that which you would call Christ-consciousness may do for you. It is true, he says, you cannot save your planet. But you, each of you, if you know at all who you are, you know that the miracle is very near, is close, and can be right now.

In your holy works, it was reported many times that the one known as Jesus performed miracles. He opened ears that could not hear and allowed the blind to see. And yet, he asks, how many of you suffer in a spiritual manner from stopped ears and blind eyes and closed hearts? Have you gone through this day in some degree unhappy? Frowning? Struggling? Then you have need of a miracle, and the miracle is very close.

What we are saying, he says, is simply that you can, at any time, make a change in your consciousness. Not by yourself, but by what you would call the grace of the spirit of love.

Now, this moment, he says, take your birthright. No man need change. The saints were only conscious of the reality of love. If you seek love, by grace you shall find it.

Through another instrument, Hatonn takes up the word love itself, and widens it until it holds everything. When we speak of love, he says, we speak of a universal concept, a concept with which all things have been created. And man of Earth looks about him and sees what is disagreeable, and labels it bad or negative. Yet in essence, that too is the love of which we speak.

Love, he says, to those who truly understand, is the tool by which they create. It is the tool or the law by which they live. In order to come into a clearer understanding, it is not only necessary to meditate daily, it is also necessary to go through the experiences and lessons of your life, and to meet that which is placed before you, whatever it may be, as a stepping stone upon which you must tread, lightly, regularly, and knowledgeably. Love the experience entirely, whether it be painful or pleasurable. For placed before you in life there is nothing of coincidence. There is only that which is intended to be learned.

There was one upon your planet with whom you are familiar, whom many call Master, he says. And that name can be yours. Learn to meet head-on all things in the light of love and you shall learn to generate within you a brightly luminous flame from the spark of divinity within you. From within you comes all things that you desire. For that love within you is the creative force of the universe. You are the light. You are the way, the knowledge, wisdom and truth. You are in the Creator as he is in you.

And the evening turned to questions. Can we receive personal guidance from you when we are alone? Can you direct us in our actions? We, as the brothers of Hatonn, will not direct or give advice at any time, he answers. But we will send to you a vibration sometimes called the conditioning wave, designed to intensify your own pathway to your higher self. This higher self, the Creator within you, may then speak to you, and it is the higher self which will direct and guide your spirit. We are only shepherds. We can point out the location of the stream. But you, and only you, may drink and be refreshed.

Can meditation provide technical insights? Each upon your planet has access to an infinite amount of knowledge, he says. Seek in the name of the Father, and seek to do service by this information. Then become very aware of those daydreams and dreams within sleep, for the channels through which information flows from the infinite mind are quite often the intuitional daydream and the visionary dream.

And one more thing, on healing. To be healed of any disease or pain, he says, it may be necessary to understand that there is no power, none whatsoever. It is the realization that disease of any type has no power that allows harmony to reassert itself. The basic force in the universe is love, with an infinite amount of energy, at all time automatically attempting to adjust all things to harmony.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Prodigal Returns
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the prodigal returns.

October third, nineteen seventy-six. Hatonn opens with the simplest message in the archive, and the reason it never arrives simply. Our message to you has always been simple, he says. We tell you that all things are love, that you are love, and that your entire existence is a process whereby your whole purpose is to become aware of your true nature; that is, to become aware of the oneness of all things and of the nature of that one thing as love. It is a simple message. Yet because your spirits are encased in flesh, he says, the simplicity is lost as it filters into your ears.

It is said in your holy works that you were created a little lower than the angels. And yet, he says, this is your particular place in the order of things. Below you is the rest of the natural creation, animals and plants, their consciousness totally within the physical plane. They are contented and very aware within that plane, and not distracted by dreams and abstractions, so they are more aware within that plane than are you. Those beings you call angels have before them always the Father's wish, so they need not choose between right and wrong, as you do. You have a difficult way to go, my brothers. You are neither flesh nor spirit, but you are both, and it is your particular task to learn how to let your spirit rule your flesh.

The Father gives free will to his children, he says, and each of us chose at one time whether we wished to go on into the realms of spirit. This is the reason of all the difficulties and pleasures of the physical plane. They are there for you to enjoy and to learn from. They are there so you can make a choice between seeing the world as an animal would, knowing only what you could see and feel, and seeing the world as spirits do, so that all things have a spiritual significance.

Now the message does not seem simple any more, does it? Now it seems a metaphysical task in which all of your thoughts have to be hauled out into the open, and you must judge each one, and it begins to seem like more trouble than it's worth. So let us go back to the simplicity, he says. All things are one. All things are love. To try to describe in your daily life the connection between your life and love, that becomes complicated. And so we tell you to meditate, to find the simplicity within the complication.

You are here for one purpose only, he says, and that is to gain knowledge, to gain understanding. This is not a selfish purpose. This is indeed your whole reason for being here. The Creator desired that each one of his children learn, of his own free will, to love him and to serve each of his brothers. Anything you may do for others must first spring from your understanding of yourself.

In your holy works, he says, it has been written that there was once a father with two sons. And one son was, as you might say, no good. The other was excellent in every respect and stayed by his father, always working, always loyal. After many years, that son that was no good came back, and the father was incredibly happy.

Each of you, we know, is in some ways a prodigal son, he says, and the Father is extremely glad to see you coming home. Each of you is a treasure beyond words to the Father. No one and no error can take away the fact that you are the son of the Father, and all that he has is yours.

Therefore, in all that you do, he says, cultivate confidence in your own basic nature, for out of confidence may spring a far different degree of ability to express those things which you know to be correct to do. Confidence causes you to relax and enjoy yourself, and we say to you that if you are enjoying yourself, then you are on the right track. The spiritual path is a narrow one, and there are many trials, but there is abundant help, for the love of the Creator is always with you. And he can lift you over the rough spots, and pick you up when you fall, bring you back when you stray.

And the evening closes with a new voice, the one known as Nona. I come to tell you simply, she says, that the universe is a place of great wonders, infinite splendor, and it is yours to explore. All that you can imagine, you can see; the farthest reaches of your thought are places you can go. Each morning that you awaken, a wonder awaits you, if you have but the eyes to see. It has been said many times, but we say it to you, it may rain, but look for the rainbow, for it is truly a beautiful, beautiful universe, and the rainbows are everywhere.

Thank you for listening.

title: Love Asks Nothing in Return
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: love asks nothing in return.

October tenth, nineteen seventy-six. Hatonn begins with the clue he says he has given time and time again. The clue, my friends, is understanding of meditation. In order to penetrate that which you call your intellect, we can only achieve a portion of true understanding through the intellectual processes. The rest comes through meditation.

You may ask, how is it that I am able to learn to love those who would not return that love? It is, he says, to be known that love is contained within you in infinite abundance, and it is replenished and multiplied by sharing with others that love within you. Love is not of a selfish nature. Love possesses nothing. Love asks nothing in return. Love is a state of consciousness which is pure and unaffected by its surroundings.

You have been given the opportunity to grow, one with the other, and to share, one with the other, your experiences and your knowledge. And you face a period of time in which your growing processes shall be speeded up. The love which you have come to realize shall now be put to the test. You, as the instrument of the infinite Creator, are to love all things constantly and infinitely. You are not to ask for the return of that love. You are to go into those situations that influence you, knowing that you shall come forth after the completion of that experience still loving those with whom you have learned.

In your life cycle you shall know many whom it shall be difficult to love. But it is necessary to have these experiences, he says, for it is easy to love those who would return that love, yet it is difficult to love those who return what you would call hate. And that difficulty is the lesson.

But here is the promise, and it is practical. You must realize, he says, that the love that you give shall indeed be returned. It may not come quickly, yet a portion of love, with what you call patience, will come. Be patient and you shall receive that which you have earned through your right actions, through your sharing of love. Turn to one another. Do what you can to help each other. Know that you are perfect; know that you are love. And be the exemplification of the love that you desire to receive.

For in this universe, like objects attract one another, he says. And for you to receive the love that you desire, it is necessary that you be that love, without fault. For if your love is faulty, so shall be that love that you receive. You are the creator of your experiences. This we have stated many times. It is time that you understood the creation in which you have placed yourselves.

Guard your thoughts, my friends. Purify your thinking processes. For your thoughts are your creations, and with them you must live. And if you desire to live in a constant environment which is agreeable to you, then so must be your love. It is possible for you to achieve, and it is your birthright. In this lifetime you can learn all that you desire. Discipline yourselves. Be the masters of your environment. Receive the assistance that is being given to you, and place not barriers about you, barriers of doubt, barriers of confusion. Know that you are protected by the infinite Creator's love. Know it without doubt. Know that you shall achieve your desire. And in truly knowing these things, they shall be done.

Through another instrument that evening, Hatonn turns to the students themselves, and the message changes from instruction to commission. We have been together for a period of time in which we have attempted to make understood to you many new concepts, he says. Now, on your plane, you may go to what is known as a school so that you may develop much knowledge in the hope that you may someday acquire enough to teach others. The time flies by, to even a quicker pace. You have learned much. Now, my friends, I do not say that you have learned so much. But it is now your place to go among your people and to teach.

For many things are understood by you which cannot be put in proper phrase, he says. As you sit and meditate, you feel this energy called love, but yet you cannot properly define it. That does not matter. We remind you again that when you leave this room, you will attempt to keep this energy vibration which you now experience at a high level throughout your day. As I have said, like entities attract each other. You will find this very valuable in acquiring new information that you will need.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Infinite Storehouse
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the infinite storehouse.

October fifteenth, nineteen seventy-six. Hatonn opens with the simple concept that is the reason for all of it. We of the Confederation are here to share with the people of your planet a very simple thought, he says. That concept is love. And yet, we have had our difficulties with your peoples. For the concept is too simple. Love, among your peoples, has become very complicated, very devious. Yet the very essence of love is that all things are one, that you and I are one, and that you and your brother are one.

In love you were created, he says, and your original vibration is pure and identical to the original vibration of all that is around you. We know that path is steep and rocky, and we ask that you take confidence in your path. Take heart in your mission to be of service and to give light, for this is truly the one thing that is of importance.

We share with you the thought, he says, that through others you may see the Creator, and others may see the Creator through you. Yet of yourself, you cannot do what you wish to do. You cannot depend upon your own resources. Yet you have infinity behind you, the storehouse of talents and power and ability so great that you can never exhaust it.

Love does not come from others, he says, nor can you call it from within your own heart. The Creator that is within you, your heart and soul, is your link to total and infinite love. Never depend upon yourself. Never shame yourself if you have been inadequate. Know only that you simply failed to ask the Creator, and next time, remember. In this way, you may meet each situation in life as a rich man who has so many assets that he cannot count them. In this quiet confidence, many things can be met with love and with graciousness, whereas if you analyzed the situation in terms of your own abilities, you would say, I cannot handle this situation, and feeling poor in spirit, the situation would overcome you. This is never necessary, for you have all that you need from the Father.

It has been written in your holy works, he says, "I have meat that ye know not of." This was said by the master known as Jesus, and he was speaking of that connection with the infinite storehouse of the Father. Those upon your planet have put value on things that can be measured. Yet all of these things that can be measured will also rust and spoil and die. And so will your physical body. So seek, each day that you can possibly find the time, for that link between yourself and the fount of all love, and at this fount, refreshed in yourself, you may always be a blessing to others.

The evening turned to questions. Asked about the difference between channeling one's own higher consciousness and channeling the brothers of the Confederation, Hatonn answers: in one way, there is no difference at all. There is no space, but only vibration. The vibration in which we exist and the vibration of your higher self is one. Our information is not ours, as such, for we are acting as conscious instruments of the Creator. We and your higher self are both imperfect.

And then he tells us why the Confederation comes at all, in this form, and it is disarmingly pragmatic. We have come to your planet not because the information is not available from your higher self, he says, but because many do not have contact with the higher self or even know of its existence. Yet many are more open to the words of one who is in a so-called flying saucer than one who is in a spiritual realm of your own planet. There are those who cannot conceive of such a thing as an angel, who can fully conceive of an extraterrestrial being. We are taking advantage of this edge to get the information to the peoples of your planet.

Asked how long they have been here, Hatonn answers: we have been coming here for thousands of your years. We have never been totally gone from your plane of existence since your history has begun to be written. At that time, there was also a situation where your peoples were at the end of a cycle in which spiritual learning was supposed to be completed, and there was a large failure to complete the lessons in time. This time, he says, it is more serious, for it is not only a minor cycle but a major cycle that is ending, so that the repetition this time is more of an investment for your spirit.
